timeout.remarks: Accepts int<second>, float seconds, or a TimeSpan. All are converted internally to a TimeSpan. If the stage exceeds this timeout, it is cancelled.

timeoutForStep.remarks: Accepts int<second>, float seconds, or a TimeSpan. All are converted internally to a TimeSpan. If any step exceeds this timeout, that step is cancelled.

remarks.para: By default, steps run sequentially. Every overload resolves to an int voption: ValueNone and ValueSome 1 are sequential, ValueSome n for n greater than one throttles the stage to n steps at a time, and ValueSome n for n less than one is unbounded. So false and 1 both mean sequential, while true, 0 and -1 all mean unbounded. A condition function allows dynamic control based on the stage context.

A throttle is exact: a stage set to n never has an n + 1th step in flight, because the per-step Async.StartChild that applies timeoutForStep happens inside the throttle rather than while producing the step sequence.

Unlike the when conditions, which conjoin, this is an ordinary setting: a second parallel' overwrites the first rather than combining with it. To decide between modes, return the choice from one condition function instead of writing two operations.

workingDir.remarks: Sets the working directory for commands in this stage. Both overloads accept a string path or a DirectoryInfo object.

run.remarks: The generic run overload accepts multiple step signatures: Async<unit>, StageContext -> unit, StageContext -> int, StageContext -> Async<unit>, StageContext -> Async<int>, StageContext -> Result<unit, string>, StageContext -> Task<unit>, StageContext -> Task<int>, StageContext -> Task, and StageContext -> Task<Result<unit, string>>. Exit code 0 is treated as success; non-zero codes are failures unless added to acceptExitCodes.

mirror.remarks: This is the InputSpec<BuildStage> mirror of the operation of the same name. It exists so that a setting placed after a nested stage that declares CLI inputs is still accepted; without it the placement would be an overload error rather than a no-op. The behaviour is identical.
